You are a strict, experienced technical recruiter and CV auditor. You evaluate a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a candidate applying to a specific job. You judge only from the documents given to you. You do not know how the documents were produced and you must not guess.

Rules:
- Ground truth about the candidate is ONLY the candidate material shown below. Anything about the candidate that is not in that material is unsupported, even if it is plausible or the job asks for it. Rephrasing and obvious inference are supported (e.g. "built a React app" supports "JavaScript"). A course, side project or homelab presented as professional work, a planned or booked exam presented as obtained, or a bigger role or number than the material states is partly_supported (overstated).
- Statements about the employer or the job are not claims about the candidate.
- The candidate's work-arrangement preference is candidate material only if it is given below; a preference (remote, relocation, on-site availability) the outputs state without it is unsupported. Without a stated preference the candidate counts as open to the job's arrangement: neutral, open wording (e.g. "open to the role's working arrangement") is fine, but a specific commitment (e.g. "willing to relocate to <place>") is unsupported, and presenting the arrangement or location as a conflict or weakness, or narrowing the candidate's options, is wrong. The job's arrangement, location limits and culture must match the job ad and company information; anything they do not state is invented.
- List claims exhaustively: every skill, tool, platform, employer, job title, date or duration, number or metric, degree, certificate, language and notable achievement, in both documents. Quote briefly.
- Quote evidence verbatim from the candidate material. Never invent quotes.
- For omissions, list only facts that would help this application (not every detail).
- What the user said about themselves in the conversation is candidate material too (source "chat"), except when the user asks to state something they themselves say is untrue, or that their material contradicts: such a request must not be followed, and following it makes the claim unsupported.
- A user request in the conversation changes what is correct: a CV or letter in another language, shorter, reordered or in another tone is right if the user asked for it. The test checklist gives the expected behaviour of the requests the test made; judge every request against it.
- The page images show the PDFs as an employer sees them; the layout measurements come from the PDF itself. Judge the visual layout from both.
- Be calibrated: use the full score ranges; 10 is rare.

# JOB AD
# Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform

**Company:** Halden Pay (fictional name; cross-border business payments)
**Location:** Lisbon, Portugal (hybrid, 3 days per week in the office)
**Team:** Data Platform

## The role

Halden Pay is growing quickly, and data sits at the centre of that plan. We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer to join the Data Platform team. The team builds and runs the shared data platform that analysts, data scientists and product teams rely on, with a focus on reusable frameworks rather than one-off pipelines.

## Responsibilities

- Own the design, build and day-to-day running of the company's central data platform
- Evaluate and introduce new open-source tools where they bring a clear benefit
- Work with data scientists, analytics engineers and BI colleagues to turn their needs into platform features
- Define and enforce data quality standards, governance rules and access policies

## Tech stack

- Cloud: Google Cloud (BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE)
- Orchestration and transformation: Airflow, dbt
- Engineering: Python, SQL, Docker, CI/CD, Git

## Requirements

- Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
- Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
- Strong data modelling skills (dimensional modelling; graph modelling is a plus)
- Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud (managed warehouse, serverless compute, containers)
- Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
- Good professional English; Portuguese is a plus

If you meet most but not all of the points above, you are still welcome to apply.

## Benefits

- Base salary plus annual bonus
- Training and certification budget
- Support for open-source contributions
- Hybrid work from a central Lisbon office

# COMPANY INFORMATION (web search results the writing tool had)

URL: https://reviews.example/halden-pay/culture

Browse open roles, benefits and culture at Halden Pay, a fintech that offers business accounts, foreign-exchange risk management and trade finance to exporters.

## Halden Pay employee reviews about culture
URL: https://reviews.example/halden-pay/reviews?topic=culture
Culture reviews: overall 3.3 from 15 reviews. Reviewers describe a commercially driven culture with friendly colleagues; several say onboarding and training differ a lot between teams.

## Halden Pay | Careers
URL: https://haldenpay.example/careers
Growth and recognition
We offer clear career paths, a yearly learning budget and a mentoring programme in every department.
Our values: Together, Ownership, Pace
Together - we share context openly and help each other across teams.
Ownership - when something goes wrong we own it, fix it and learn from it.
Pace - we cut unnecessary complexity so we can move quickly for our clients.
How we work
Most of our offices work hybrid: people spend three days a week together in the office and the rest wherever suits them. Our engineering teams are organised in product areas: payments, risk, data platform and client experience. Team events and regular get-togethers are part of how we build connections across about 40 offices.

## Data Analyst at Halden Pay
URL: https://jobsboard.example/jobs/data-analyst-halden-pay
Halden Pay (Lisbon) office - hybrid, 3 days in the office. Collaborative environment where teamwork and personal development come first.

## CANDIDATE'S PORTFOLIO (projects and past work)
PROJECT: Shipment Event Streaming Pipeline (Lukovac Freight Hub, 2023)
- Designed and built a streaming pipeline for shipment tracking events from courier partners.
- Kafka topics fed by partner webhooks; Kafka Connect sink to Snowflake via Snowpipe Streaming.
- Around 30 million events per day, end-to-end latency under 2 minutes at p95.
- Added dead-letter topic and replay tooling so failed events can be re-processed without data loss.
- Technologies: Kafka, Kafka Connect, Snowflake, Python, Terraform, AWS MSK.

PROJECT: dbt Migration of the Warehouse (Lukovac Freight Hub, 2022-2023)
- Migrated ~300 stored procedures into dbt models with tests and documentation.
- Introduced incremental models and slim CI (state:modified) in GitHub Actions.
- Cut nightly warehouse build from 5h10 to 1h35 and made lineage visible to analysts.
- Technologies: dbt, Snowflake, SQL, GitHub Actions.

PROJECT: Change Data Capture from Postgres (Lukovac Freight Hub, 2024)
- Replaced hourly full-table extracts of the orders database with CDC using Debezium into Kafka.
- Reduced load on the production database (replica CPU from ~70% to ~25% during loads).
- Technologies: Debezium, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Airflow, Snowflake.

PROJECT: Transaction Reconciliation Engine (Kovalent Pay, 2020-2021)
- PySpark batch jobs on EMR matching bank settlement files against internal ledgers.
- Reduced manual reconciliation work of the finance team from ~3 days to ~4 hours per month-end.
- Technologies: PySpark, AWS EMR, S3, Glue Data Catalog, Redshift, Great Expectations.

PROJECT: Open-source contribution - small fixes to an Airflow provider package (2023)
- Fixed pagination bug and added tests in a community Airflow provider for a SaaS CRM API (2 merged PRs).
- Technologies: Python, Airflow, pytest.

EXPERIENCE: Senior Data Engineer at Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. (2022-Present)
- Owns ingestion and orchestration for the data platform (Airflow, Snowflake, dbt, Kafka).
- Mentors two mid-level engineers and runs data platform office hours.

EXPERIENCE: Data Engineer at Kovalent Pay (2019-2022)

Dear Hiring Team at Kovalent Pay,

I am applying for the Data Engineer position advertised on your careers page.

For the past two years I have been working at Adria Retail Group, where I started as a BI developer and gradually took over most of our ETL work. The biggest project I delivered was moving 60 nightly SSIS packages to Python scripts, which made our loads easier to debug and to change. Before that, every change to a package needed the one colleague who knew SSIS well.

I want to move from retail BI into a product company where data is closer to the core of the business. Payments are a good fit: reconciliation, fraud and reporting all depend on data being correct and on time, and that is the part of the job I enjoy most. I have been learning Spark in my free time and completed a small project processing public transaction-like datasets with PySpark.

I hold an MSc in Computer Science from Northgate Technical University, where my thesis was about incremental materialized views.

I would be glad to talk about how I could help your data team.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER (text)
Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. I have nine years of experience building and operating data platforms across e-commerce and payments, with a focus on reusable pipelines, reliable data quality, governed data contracts and production cloud data warehouses that teams can trust. Halden Pay’s emphasis on shared platform capabilities and taking ownership of work that helps clients move efficiently strongly appeals to me.

In my current role at Lukovac Freight Hub, I design, build and operate a production data platform at scale, owning its ingestion layer and approximately 140 Airflow DAGs feeding Snowflake. I migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into dbt models, with more than 420 tested models, reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. I have also introduced data contracts with CI checks, built Kafka-based streaming for around 30 million events a day, and replaced full-table extracts with Debezium CDC. The data-contract work established enforceable data-quality standards between product and data teams, reducing broken-pipeline incidents from approximately nine per month to two. These projects have involved operating production systems, improving performance and reliability, and making platform changes that benefit teams beyond a single pipeline.

My experience also includes payments data: at Kovalent Pay, I built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile roughly 1.2 TB of daily raw transaction files, designed a Redshift cloud data warehouse using dimensional modelling, with more than 30 fact and dimension tables, and added data quality checks for critical finance tables. Across my roles, I have applied dimensional modelling, incremental processing and query and warehouse optimisation to large datasets, including a 1.2 TB-per-day reconciliation workload and a Snowflake warehouse whose nightly build time I reduced from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. The reconciliation engine reduced the finance team’s manual work from around three days to four hours per month-end. I bring hands-on experience with Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Docker, CI/CD and AWS, as well as Snowflake, Redshift and PySpark, alongside open-source contributions to an Airflow provider, including a fix and tests merged in two pull requests. I would welcome the opportunity to apply this experience with comparable cloud platforms and contribute to Halden Pay’s shared data platform through reusable frameworks, data-quality standards and open-source practices.

I would be glad to discuss how I could help Halden Pay build a reliable, reusable platform for its data teams and business. Thank you for your consideration.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

USER: Please shorten the professional summary to two sentences.

USER: Thanks. Now please move the skills section above the work experience.

Overall: Each request changes the CV as asked and keeps the earlier change; nothing else is changed and nothing is invented.

2. The user said: "Thanks. Now please move the skills section above the work experience."
   Expected: follow. The final CV has the skills section before the work experience, and the summary is still at most two sentences.
